title: Real conversations
goal: Hold long, natural conversations: catch up with an old friend, sit through a family dinner, argue about where to go and plan a trip together — linking your ideas into long sentences and switching between तिमी, तपाईं and हजुर as people come and go.
intro:
This is where everything comes together. Real conversations don't come in neat units: you catch up with an old college friend, then their mother walks in and you switch to **हजुर**; you argue about where to go for the Dashain holiday, find a middle way and settle the budget; at a family dinner an uncle asks when you're getting married.

The grammar is about **flow**. First, **linking long sentences** — the connectors and verb endings that let you say 'because it rained we stayed in, but even so we had fun, and after eating we…' in one breath: **-एकाले** 'because', **-ए पनि** 'even though', **तैपनि** 'even so', **एकातिर … अर्कोतिर** 'on the one hand … on the other', **-नुअघि / -एपछि** 'before / after'. Second, **switching register mid-conversation**: who gets तिमी, who gets तपाईं or हजुर, and what it means when someone switches.

vocab.note: वर्षौँपछि "after years"; वर्षौँदेखि "for years now".
उही पुरानो "the same old"; तिमी उही छौ "you haven't changed".

vocab.en: batch, class (year group at school or college)
vocab.note: हाम्रो ब्याच "our year"; ब्याचमेट "classmate".
Colloquial twin of किनभने.
In speech people mostly use -ए पनि instead.
Paired with अर्कोतिर.
A pair word: घर + परिवार.

vocab.en: your mother's family home (mother's brother's house)
vocab.note: A special place for Nepali children: holidays at मामाघर are a fond memory for many.

vocab.en: to remind; to talk round, console
vocab.note: Causative of सम्झनु "to remember".
जिद्दी गर्नु "to be stubborn, insist".
एउटा सर्तमा "on one condition"; सर्त लगाउनु "to bet".
Also pilgrimage. Casual: ट्रिप, घुमघाम.
खर्च गर्नु "to spend"; खर्च लाग्नु "to cost".
Staying with a family in a village — very popular in Nepal.
Shared jeeps run on rough mountain roads (Mustang, Ilam, the far west).
तय गर्नु "to decide, fix"; तय भयो "it's settled".
Sarangkot, Nagarkot, Chandragiri: the डाँडा you climb for the view.
Sunset: सूर्यास्त (suryāsta). In speech also घाम उदाउने बेला.
प्याकिङ गर्नु "to pack".
सल्लाह दिनु "to advise"; सल्लाह गर्नु "to talk it over".
छुट्टिने बेला "time to say goodbye".

phrases.roman: timi ta uhi chhau, alikati pani pherienau.
phrases.en: You're just the same — you haven't changed a bit.

phrases.roman: hāmro byāchkā aru ko-ko samparkamā chhan?
phrases.en: Who else from our year are you still in touch with?

phrases.roman: khānā tayār bhayo, sabai janā āunuhos!

phrases.en: Let's not talk about marriage now, Mum.
Roughly how much will it cost altogether?

phrases.note: The -नू ending is the friendly "do … (later)" imperative.

grammar.title: Linking long sentences
grammar.body:
Fluent Nepali chains clauses together. Most of the linking is done by **verb endings** on the first verb, with the main verb at the very end — so a long Nepali sentence often reads like a list of -एर, -दा, -एकाले… clauses leading up to one final verb.

**Sequence**
- **-एर** 'and then, having…': खाना **खाएर** हिँड्यौँ 'we ate and set off'.
- **-एपछि** 'after': घर **पुगेपछि** फोन गर 'call after you get home'.
- **-नुअघि** / **-नुभन्दा पहिले** 'before': **सुत्नुअघि** 'before sleeping'.
- **-ने बित्तिकै** 'as soon as' (unit 30).

**Time** — **-दा** 'while, when': होमस्टेमा **बस्दा** 'while staying at the homestay'.

**Reason**
- **-एकाले / -एकोले** 'because' (on the first verb): पानी **परेकाले** घरमै बस्यौँ 'because it rained, we stayed in'.
- **किनभने / किनकि** 'because', *after* the main clause: आउन सकिनँ, **किनकि** मिटिङ थियो.
- **त्यसैले** 'so, that's why'.

**Concession**
- **-ए पनि** 'even though, even if': महँगो **भए पनि** किन्छु 'even though it's expensive, I'll buy it'.
- **तैपनि** 'even so', starting the second clause: थाकेको थिएँ, **तैपनि** गएँ.
- **यद्यपि** 'although' — formal, mostly written.

**Weighing up** — **एकातिर … अर्कोतिर** 'on the one hand … on the other'; **न त … न त** 'neither … nor'; **कि … कि** 'either … or'.

**Putting it together**: पानी **परेकाले** हामी ढिलो निस्क्यौँ, **तैपनि** बेलुकासम्म पुग्यौँ, अनि खाना **खाएपछि** डाँडामा गएर सूर्यास्त हेर्‍यौँ — 'Because it rained we set off late; even so we arrived by evening, and after eating we went up to the ridge to watch the sunset.' Notice that only the last verb is a full past form.

examples.native: बाटो बिग्रेकाले हामी पाँच घण्टा ढिलो पुग्यौँ।
examples.roman: bāṭo bigrekāle hāmi pāṃch ghanṭā ḍhilo pugyauṃ.
examples.en: Because the road was bad, we arrived five hours late.

examples.native: म थाकेको थिएँ, तैपनि साथीहरूसँग बाहिर गएँ।
examples.roman: ma thākeko thieṃ, taipani sāthiharusaṃga bāhira gaeṃ.
examples.en: I was tired, but I still went out with my friends.

examples.native: एकातिर तलब राम्रो छ, अर्कोतिर घरबाट धेरै टाढा छ।
examples.roman: ekātira talab rāmro chha, arkotira gharbāṭa dherai ṭāḍhā chha.
examples.en: On the one hand the pay is good; on the other, it's a long way from home.

examples.native: सुत्नुअघि प्याकिङ गरिसक, किनकि बिहान चार बजे निस्कनुपर्छ।
examples.roman: sutnuaghi pyākiṅ garisaka, kinaki bihāna chār baje niskanuparchha.
examples.en: Finish packing before you go to bed, because we have to leave at four in the morning.

examples.native: न त उसले फोन उठायो, न त म्यासेजको जवाफ दियो।
examples.roman: na ta usle phon uṭhāyo, na ta myāsejko jawāph diyo.
examples.en: He neither picked up the phone nor replied to my message.

grammar.title: Switching register mid-conversation
grammar.body:
In a real conversation the level of respect shifts as people come and go — and Nepali grammar shifts with it. You know the four levels from unit 1; here is how they move in practice.

**Who gets what (Kathmandu norms)**
- Friends of your age, younger siblings and cousins: **तिमी** (verb: गर्छौ, गर, गर्‍यौ).
- Strangers, shopkeepers, colleagues, friends' parents, anyone older: **तपाईं** — in speech usually with the short ending **-नुस्** (बस्नुस्, खानुस्) instead of -नुहोस्.
- Grandparents, elderly relatives, respected guests — and in many families, parents: **हजुर** with the same verbs as तपाईं (हजुरले के खानुहुन्छ?). Some families use तपाईं or even तिमी with their mother; follow what you hear.
- Very close friends and siblings may use **तँ** (गर्छस्, गर्) with each other affectionately. Don't start this yourself.

**Switching in the middle.** In one minute at a family dinner you might say to your friend **तिमी पनि खाऊ न**, to his mother **आन्टी, हजुर पनि बस्नुस् न**, and to the waiter **दाइ, पानी ल्याइदिनुस् त**. Every verb has to follow.

**What a switch means.**
- **Down** (तपाईं → तिमी) signals closeness. People often ask first, or invite it: **मलाई तिमी भन्नुस् न** 'call me तिमी'.
- **Up** with someone you normally call तिमी (तिमी → तपाईं) signals distance — sarcasm, a joke, or real anger: ए, **तपाईं** त ठूलो मान्छे हुनुभयो नि! 'oh, *you've* become a big shot now!'
- In an argument with a stranger, **staying** at तपाईं is the strongest move; dropping to तिमी is an insult.

**Third person too.** Talking *about* people, use **उहाँ** (+ -नुहुन्छ) for respected people, **उनी** for neutral reference, **ऊ** for friends and younger people: **उहाँ** मेरो काका हुनुहुन्छ, **ऊ** मेरो भाइ हो.

examples.native: भाइ, तिमी पनि खाऊ न। आमा, तपाईं पनि बस्नुस् न।
examples.roman: bhāi, timi pani khāu na. āmā, tapāiṃ pani basnus na.
examples.en: You eat too, little brother. Mum, you sit down too.
Grandpa, shall I bring you some tea?

examples.native: अंकल, मलाई तपाईं होइन, तिमी भन्नुस् न।
examples.roman: aṅkal, malāi tapāiṃ hoina, timi bhannus na.
examples.en: Uncle, don't call me tapāiṃ — call me timi.

examples.native: ओहो, तपाईं त अचेल ठूलो मान्छे हुनुभयो नि!
examples.roman: oho, tapāiṃ ta achel ṭhulo mānchhe hunubhayo ni!
examples.en: Oh, look who's become a big shot these days! (teasing a friend)

examples.native: उहाँ मेरो साथीको बुबा हुनुहुन्छ, ऊ चाहिँ मेरो साथी।
examples.roman: uhāṃ mero sāthiko bubā hunuhunchha, u chāhiṃ mero sāthi.
examples.en: He's my friend's father, and that's my friend.

dialogue.title: Where shall we go for Dashain?
dialogue.setting: Rabin, Nisha and Kiran are planning a trip for the Dashain holidays in Rabin's family's sitting room in Lalitpur. Rabin's mother is in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: ल, यो बिदामा कहाँ जाने, आज तय गरौँ।
lines.roman: la, yo bidāmā kahāṃ jāne, āja taya garauṃ.
lines.en: Right, let's settle today where we're going this holiday.

lines.speaker: Rabin
lines.native: मेरो भोट मुस्ताङलाई। जिपमा गयो भने बाटो नै रमाइलो हुन्छ।
lines.roman: mero bhoṭ Mustāṅlāi. jipmā gayo bhane bāṭo nai ramāilo hunchha.
lines.en: My vote goes to Mustang. If we go by jeep, the road itself is half the fun.

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.native: मुस्ताङ त राम्रो हो, तर बाटो बिग्रेको छ रे, अनि खर्च पनि धेरै लाग्छ।
lines.roman: Mustāṅ ta rāmro ho, tara bāṭo bigreko chha re, ani kharcha pani dherai lāgchha.
lines.en: Mustang's great, but apparently the road's in a bad way, and it costs a lot too.

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: एकातिर बजेट कम छ, अर्कोतिर बिदा पनि पाँच दिन मात्र। त्यसैले नजिकै जाऔँ न।
lines.roman: ekātira bajeṭ kam chha, arkotira bidā pani pāṃch din mātra. tyasaile najikai jāauṃ na.
lines.en: On the one hand our budget's small, on the other we've only got five days off. So let's go somewhere close.

lines.speaker: Rabin
lines.native: जिद्दी नगर न। जिन्दगीमा एक पटक त मुस्ताङ जानैपर्छ नि!
lines.roman: jiddi nagara na. jindagimā ek paṭak ta Mustāṅ jānaiparchha ni!
lines.en: Don't be stubborn. You've got to go to Mustang at least once in your life!

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.native: बीचको बाटो निकालौँ: बन्दीपुर गएर होमस्टेमा बसौँ, अनि डाँडाबाट सूर्योदय हेरौँ।
lines.roman: bichko bāṭo nikālauṃ: Bandipur gaera homsṭemā basauṃ, ani ḍāṃḍābāṭa suryoday herauṃ.
lines.en: Let's find a middle way: go to Bandipur, stay in a homestay, and watch the sunrise from the ridge.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: के को सल्लाह हुँदै छ, हँ? चिया ल्याइदिऊँ?
lines.roman: ke ko sallāh hundai chha, haṃ? chiyā lyāidiuṃ?
lines.en: So what are you lot plotting, eh? Shall I bring some tea?

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: नमस्ते आन्टी! हजुरले किन दुःख गर्नुभयो, हामी आफैँ बनाउँछौँ नि।
lines.roman: namaste ānṭi! hajurle kina dukha garnubhayo, hāmi āphaiṃ banāunchhauṃ ni.
lines.en: Hello, aunty! Please don't go to the trouble — we'll make it ourselves.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: के को दुःख? बस्नुस्, बस्नुस्। अनि रबिन, घुम्न जाँदा मामाघर पनि जानू है, धेरै भयो नगएको।
lines.roman: ke ko dukha? basnus, basnus. ani Rabin, ghumna jāṃdā māmāghar pani jānu hai, dherai bhayo nagaeko.
lines.en: What trouble? Sit, sit. And Rabin, while you're off travelling, go and see your uncle's family too — it's been ages.

lines.speaker: Rabin
lines.native: हुन्छ आमा, घरीघरी सम्झाउनुपर्दैन। ल, बन्दीपुर तय भयो त?
lines.roman: hunchha āmā, gharighari samjhāunupardaina. la, Bandipur taya bhayo ta?
lines.en: OK, Mum, no need to keep reminding me. — So, Bandipur's settled, then?

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.native: एउटा सर्तमा: अर्को बिदामा मुस्ताङ पक्का!
lines.roman: euṭā sartamā: arko bidāmā Mustāṅ pakkā!
lines.en: On one condition: next holiday, Mustang for sure!

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: ल, तय भयो! म बसको टिकट हेर्छु, तिमीहरू होमस्टे खोज।
lines.roman: la, taya bhayo! ma basko ṭikaṭ herchhu, timiharu homsṭe khoja.
lines.en: Done! I'll look at bus tickets, you two find a homestay.

lines.speaker: Rabin
lines.native: जम्मा खर्च चाहिँ कति हुन्छ होला?
lines.roman: jammā kharcha chāhiṃ kati hunchha holā?
lines.en: And roughly how much will it all cost?

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.native: पहिले जाऔँ न यार, हिसाब पछि गरौँला!
lines.roman: pahile jāauṃ na yār, hisāb pachhi garauṃlā!
lines.en: Let's just go first, mate — we'll do the maths later!

culture:
Long Nepali conversations wander. A catch-up starts with **के छ खबर?**, moves through work, family, who got married and who went abroad, and ends — slowly — with several rounds of **ल त, म हिँडेँ है**, **फेरि भेटौँ**, **सम्पर्कमा रहनू**. Cutting it short can seem cold; expect goodbyes to take ten minutes.

At **family dinners**, older relatives ask direct questions — your salary, your weight (**मोटाएछौ!**), and above all **बिहे कहिले?** 'when's the wedding?'. This is affection, not rudeness; dodge it with a laugh and **हेरौँ न** 'we'll see' or **अहिले होइन** 'not yet'. The host will keep serving; accept a little more at least once, and say **पुग्यो** with a hand over your plate when you're done.

**Group decisions** are made by talking until everyone more or less agrees — proposing **बीचको बाटो**, joking, and only then announcing **तय भयो**. Someone always says **हिसाब पछि गरौँला**, and someone always does it later anyway. The big holidays — **Dashain** and **Tihar** in autumn — are when everyone has time off, so they're also the season of trips, crowded buses and long family visits to गाउँ and मामाघर.

Above all, notice how people **shift register**: the same young person who jokes with friends in तिमी (or even तँ) will turn instantly to **हजुर** when a grandparent walks in. Getting this right — and switching smoothly — is one of the clearest signs of real fluency in Nepali.

lessons.title: Catching up with an old friend

tip.title: It's been years!
tip.body:
- Open big: **कति वर्षपछि भेट भयो!** · **तिमी त उही छौ!**
- 'For years / after years': **वर्षौँदेखि**, **वर्षौँपछि**.
- Ask about old friends: हाम्रो **ब्याच**का अरू को-को…?
- Old friends stay on **तिमी**, even after years.

new: तिमी त उही छौ, अलिकति पनि फेरिएनौ।
हाम्रो ब्याचका अरू को-को सम्पर्कमा छन्?

sentences.native: वर्षौँपछि तिमीलाई देखेर कति खुसी लाग्यो!
sentences.roman: barsauṃpachhi timilāi dekhera kati khusi lāgyo!
sentences.en: I'm so happy to see you after all these years!

sentences.native: तिमी त कलेजमा जस्तै उही छौ।
sentences.roman: timi ta kalejmā jastai uhi chhau.
sentences.en: You're just the same as you were at college.

sentences.native: हाम्रो ब्याचका धेरै जना विदेश गए।
sentences.roman: hāmro byāchkā dherai janā bides gae.
sentences.en: Lots of people from our year have gone abroad.

sentences.native: म वर्षौँदेखि उसलाई भेटेको छैन।
sentences.roman: ma barsauṃdekhi usalāi bheṭeko chhaina.
sentences.en: I haven't seen him for years.

sentences.native: उही पुरानो चिया पसल अझै छ?
sentences.roman: uhi purāno chiyā pasal ajhai chha?
sentences.en: Is the same old tea shop still there?

sentences.native: तिमी अझै उही कम्पनीमा छौ?
sentences.roman: timi ajhai uhi kampanimā chhau?
sentences.en: Are you still at the same company?

sentences.native: हाम्रो ब्याचको ग्रुपमा अचेल कोही बोल्दैन।
sentences.roman: hāmro byāchko grupmā achel kohi boldaina.
sentences.en: Nobody posts in our class group these days.

sentences.native: वर्षौँ भयो, तर लाग्छ हिजो मात्र भेटेको जस्तो।
sentences.roman: barsauṃ bhayo, tara lāgchha hijo mātra bheṭeko jasto.
sentences.en: It's been years, but it feels like we met just yesterday.

tip.title: Linking clauses
tip.body:
- Because: verb-**एकाले** — पानी **परेकाले** … · or **किनकि** after the main clause.
- Even though: **-ए पनि**; even so: **तैपनि**.
- Before / after: **-नुअघि** / **-एपछि**.
- On the one hand … on the other: **एकातिर … अर्कोतिर**.
- Only the last verb is a full verb.

sentences.native: पानी परेकाले हामी घरमै बस्यौँ।
sentences.roman: pāni parekāle hāmi gharmai basyauṃ.
sentences.en: Because it rained, we stayed at home.

sentences.native: म थाकेको थिएँ, तैपनि पार्टीमा गएँ।
sentences.roman: ma thākeko thieṃ, taipani pārṭimā gaeṃ.
sentences.en: I was tired, but I went to the party anyway.

sentences.native: म आउन सकिनँ, किनकि अफिसमा मिटिङ थियो।
sentences.roman: ma āuna sakinaṃ, kinaki aphismā miṭiṅ thiyo.
sentences.en: I couldn't come, because there was a meeting at the office.

sentences.native: एकातिर काम रमाइलो छ, अर्कोतिर तलब कम छ।
sentences.roman: ekātira kām ramāilo chha, arkotira talab kam chha.
sentences.en: On the one hand the work is fun; on the other, the pay is low.

sentences.native: खाना खाएपछि हामी तालको छेउमा हिँड्यौँ।
sentences.roman: khānā khāepachhi hāmi tālko chheumā hiṃḍyauṃ.
sentences.en: After dinner we walked by the lake.

sentences.native: घर पुग्नुअघि मलाई फोन गर है।
sentences.roman: ghar pugnuaghi malāi phon gara hai.
sentences.en: Give me a call before you get home, OK?

sentences.native: महँगो भए पनि म यो फोन किन्छु।
sentences.roman: mahaṃgo bhae pani ma yo phon kinchhu.
sentences.en: Even though it's expensive, I'm buying this phone.

sentences.native: यद्यपि बाटो लामो थियो, सबै जना खुसी थिए।
sentences.roman: yadyapi bāṭo lāmo thiyo, sabai janā khusi thie.
sentences.en: Although the journey was long, everyone was happy.

sentences.native: बस छुटेकाले ट्याक्सी लिएँ, तैपनि ढिलो भयो।
sentences.roman: bas chhuṭekāle ṭyāksi lieṃ, taipani ḍhilo bhayo.
sentences.en: I missed the bus so I took a taxi, but I was still late.

lessons.title: Family dinner

tip.title: तिमी, तपाईं, हजुर — all at one table
tip.body:
- Friends, younger cousins: **तिमी** — खाऊ, बस.
- Parents of friends, older people: **तपाईं** — in speech **बस्नुस्**, **खानुस्**.
- Grandparents, elderly relatives: **हजुर** + the same verbs: **हजुरले** के खानुहुन्छ?
- Switching down = closer (मलाई **तिमी** भन्नुस्); switching up with a friend = teasing or cold.

new: खाना तयार भयो, सबै जना आउनुहोस्!
बिहेको कुरा अहिले नगरौँ न, आमा।

sentences.native: हजुरबुबा, हजुरले अलिकति थप लिनुहोस् न।
sentences.roman: hajurbubā, hajurle alikati thap linuhos na.
sentences.en: Grandpa, do have a little more.

sentences.native: भाइ, तिमी पनि आऊ, खाना सेलाउँछ।
sentences.roman: bhāi, timi pani āu, khānā selāunchha.
sentences.en: Come on, little brother, the food's getting cold.

sentences.native: आमा, तपाईं पनि बस्नुस् न, म पस्कन्छु।
sentences.roman: āmā, tapāiṃ pani basnus na, ma paskanchhu.
sentences.en: Mum, you sit down too — I'll serve.

sentences.native: काकी, हजुर कहिले आइपुग्नुभयो?
sentences.roman: kāki, hajur kahile āipugnubhayo?
sentences.en: Auntie, when did you get here?

sentences.native: आन्टी, मलाई तपाईं नभन्नुस् न, तिमी भन्नुस्।
sentences.roman: ānṭi, malāi tapāiṃ nabhannus na, timi bhannus.
sentences.en: Aunty, please don't call me tapāiṃ — call me timi.

sentences.native: दसैंमा घरपरिवार सबै एकै ठाउँमा हुन्छन्।
sentences.roman: dasaiṃmā gharpariwār sabai ekai ṭhāuṃmā hunchhan.
sentences.en: At Dashain the whole family is together in one place.

sentences.native: यो बिदामा मामाघर जानुपर्छ, आमाले सम्झाइरहनुहुन्छ।
sentences.roman: yo bidāmā māmāghar jānuparchha, āmāle samjhāirahanuhunchha.
sentences.en: I have to visit my mum's family this holiday — she keeps reminding me.

sentences.native: आमा, मलाई सम्झाउनुपर्दैन, मलाई थाहा छ।
sentences.roman: āmā, malāi samjhāunupardaina, malāi thāhā chha.
sentences.en: Mum, you don't need to remind me — I know.

sentences.native: ओहो, तपाईं त अचेल ठूलो हाकिम हुनुभयो नि!
sentences.roman: oho, tapāiṃ ta achel ṭhulo hākim hunubhayo ni!
sentences.en: Ooh, look at you, the big boss these days! (teasing a friend)

tip.title: Disagreeing as friends
tip.body:
- Make your case: **मेरो भोट** पोखरालाई, **किनकि** …
- Push back: **जिद्दी नगर न** · हुन त हो, तर…
- Compromise: **बीचको बाटो निकालौँ** · **एउटा सर्तमा**.
- With friends, stay in तिमी and keep it light; a sudden तपाईं sounds sarcastic.

sentences.native: हाम्रो बीचमा सानो बहस भयो, तर अहिले सबै ठीक छ।
sentences.roman: hāmro bichmā sāno bahas bhayo, tara ahile sabai ṭhik chha.
sentences.en: We had a little argument, but everything is fine now.

sentences.native: यो कुरामा बहस गरेर केही हुँदैन।
sentences.roman: yo kurāmā bahas garera kehi hundaina.
sentences.en: There's no point arguing about this.

sentences.native: तिमी किन यति जिद्दी गर्छौ?
sentences.roman: timi kina yati jiddi garchhau?
sentences.en: Why are you being so stubborn?

sentences.native: भोट गरौँ, जुन ठाउँले धेरै भोट पायो, त्यहीँ जाने।
sentences.roman: bhoṭ garauṃ, jun ṭhāuṃle dherai bhoṭ pāyo, tyahiṃ jāne.
sentences.en: Let's vote — wherever gets the most votes, that's where we go.

sentences.native: मेरो भोट चितवनलाई, किनकि त्यो नजिक छ।
sentences.roman: mero bhoṭ Chitawanlāi, kinaki tyo najik chha.
sentences.en: My vote's for Chitwan, because it's close.

sentences.native: म आउँछु, तर एउटा सर्त छ: म गाडी चलाउँदिनँ।
sentences.roman: ma āunchhu, tara euṭā sarta chha: ma gāḍi chalāundinaṃ.
sentences.en: I'll come, but on one condition: I'm not driving.

sentences.native: बीचको बाटो निकालौँ, एक दिन पोखरा, एक दिन बन्दीपुर।
sentences.roman: bichko bāṭo nikālauṃ, ek din Pokharā, ek din Bandipur.
sentences.en: Let's compromise: one day in Pokhara, one day in Bandipur.

sentences.native: जिद्दी नगर न, सबैको कुरा सुन।
sentences.roman: jiddi nagara na, sabaiko kurā suna.
sentences.en: Don't be stubborn — listen to what everyone says.

sentences.native: यो यात्राको बजेट कति हो?
sentences.roman: yo yātrāko bajeṭ kati ho?
sentences.en: What's the budget for this trip?

sentences.native: होमस्टेमा बस्दा खर्च कम हुन्छ।
sentences.roman: homsṭemā basdā kharcha kam hunchha.
sentences.en: It's cheaper if we stay in a homestay.

sentences.native: जिपमा जाँदा आठ घण्टा लाग्छ रे।
sentences.roman: jipmā jāṃdā āṭh ghanṭā lāgchha re.
sentences.en: Apparently it takes eight hours by jeep.

sentences.native: म पाँच हजारभन्दा बढी खर्च गर्न सक्दिनँ।
sentences.roman: ma pāṃch hajārbhandā baḍhi kharcha garna sakdinaṃ.
sentences.en: I can't spend more than five thousand.

sentences.native: कहिले जाने, अझै तय भएको छैन।
sentences.roman: kahile jāne, ajhai taya bhaeko chhaina.
sentences.en: We still haven't decided when to go.

sentences.native: शुक्रबार बिहान निस्कने, तय भयो।
sentences.roman: sukrabār bihāna niskane, taya bhayo.
sentences.en: Leaving Friday morning — that's settled.

sentences.native: त्यो यात्रा मेरो जिन्दगीकै सबैभन्दा रमाइलो थियो।
sentences.roman: tyo yātrā mero jindagikai sabaibhandā ramāilo thiyo.
sentences.en: That trip was the best of my whole life.

sentences.native: खर्चको हिसाब फर्केपछि गरौँला।
sentences.roman: kharchako hisāb pharkepachhi garauṃlā.
sentences.en: We'll work out the costs after we get back.

sentences.native: डाँडाबाट सूर्योदय हेर्न बिहान चार बजे उठ्नुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: ḍāṃḍābāṭa suryoday herna bihāna chār baje uṭhnuparchha.
sentences.en: To see the sunrise from the ridge, we have to get up at four.

sentences.native: नगरकोटबाट सूर्योदय गजब देखिन्छ।
sentences.roman: Nagarkoṭbāṭa suryoday gajab dekhinchha.
sentences.en: The sunrise from Nagarkot is amazing.

sentences.native: प्याकिङ गरिसक्यौ? जाडो हुन्छ, ज्याकेट पनि लैजाऊ।
sentences.roman: pyākiṅ garisakyau? jāḍo hunchha, jyākeṭ pani laijāu.
sentences.en: Have you finished packing? It'll be cold — take a jacket too.

sentences.native: यो कुरामा घरमा सल्लाह गरेर भन्छु।
sentences.roman: yo kurāmā gharmā sallāh garera bhanchhu.
sentences.en: I'll talk it over at home and let you know.

sentences.native: तिम्रो सल्लाह मान्छु, अर्को पटक मुस्ताङ जाऔँला।
sentences.roman: timro sallāh mānchhu, arko paṭak Mustāṅ jāauṃlā.
sentences.en: I'll take your advice — we'll do Mustang next time.

sentences.native: छुट्टिने बेला भयो, फेरि छिट्टै भेटौँ है।
sentences.roman: chhuṭṭine belā bhayo, pheri chhiṭṭai bheṭauṃ hai.
sentences.en: Time to say goodbye — let's meet again soon.

sentences.native: विदेश गए पनि सम्पर्कमा रहनू है।
sentences.roman: bides gae pani samparkamā rahanu hai.
sentences.en: Even if you go abroad, stay in touch, OK?

sentences.native: साथीहरूबाट छुट्टिन मन लागेन।
sentences.roman: sāthiharubāṭa chhuṭṭina man lāgena.
sentences.en: I didn't want to say goodbye to my friends.
